title: IN-FLIGHT ELECTRO-STATIC DISCHARGE MONITOR FOR SPACECRAFT - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop non-intrusive sensors for the characterization of Electro-Static Discharge on Spacecraft (e.g. for LEO constellations) together with an on-board events detection algorithm based on advanced approaches (e.g. AI based).Description: Electro-Static Discharge (ESD) phenomena on spacecraft have been estimated to contribute to around 20% to 25% of satellites anomalies overall.Yet, in-flight characterization of spacecraft ESDs in-flight has never been undertaken in a systematic way. In addition, while mitigation strategies are known for classical s/c configurations, new technologies (e.g. flexible solar arrays) require specific characterization in terms of risk (including in-flight) in order to demonstrate their maturity. The need for ensuring European space assetsresilience in LEO combined with the trend to mass product, fly and operate low power low mass constellation satellites calls for efficient and standardized environmental effects diagnostics, among which the one proposed here. The occurrence of ESDson Spacecraft in-flight depends on specific spacecraft electrical configurations and coupling with environments. LEO constellations growing market are subject to such risk as reported in the case of present constellations with thousands of events observed in flight (GEO (telecom, earth observation), MEO (navigation, orbit raising), as well as SSO polar environments also present a risk in that respect) due toboth surface and internal charging. From there, identifying relevant probing location on spacecraft systems where to systematicallyaccommodate non-intrusive /low resources sensors (e.g. current probes and well located RF receivers) would be of high interest to primes, spacecraft designers and agencies to improve our understanding of ESD phenomena in space and its relation to anomalies. In particular, the systematic integration of such sensors on low resource low mass constellation elements should enable large scale environmental effects diagnostics and improve the constellations resilience. title: RISC-V INSTRUCTION SET ARCHITECTURE SIMULATION MODEL AND EMULATION IN VIRTUAL PLATFORM FOR HARDWARE-SOFTWARE CODESIGN - EXPRO PLUS
description: The objective of this activity is to develop a simulation model of a RISC-V (reduced instruction set computer) instruction set architecture (ISA) processor and peripherals, in a suitable hardware-software co-design environment, and perform design space exploration of a system-on-chip.Description:RISC-V is an open-source and royalty-free hardware instruction set architecture based on RISC principles. An open ISA is remarkably interesting for space due to several reasons: It reduces potential difficulties in license negotiation or export restrictions. It allows to perform modifications for radiation mitigation. It adds or modifies instructions to execute functions that are frequently required by space applications, such as bit manipulation, sub-word arithmetic, vector or SIMD (single instruction, multiple data) computations.RISC-V has been gaining popularity in the past years, and its use in space is now close to a reality thanks to several on-going system-on-chip (SoC) developments that will embed RISC-V multi core processor, along with several other interfaces to enable their use in satellite payloads and platforms, such as SpaceFibre, TM/TC (telemetry/telecommand) or cryptographic functions. The successful adoption of this architecture and embarking of the future SoC depends in a great extent on the features of the hardware, and on the availability of software development tool chains that enable the programming of the cores with suitable on-board software.Hardware and software developments around RISC-V can benefit greatly from the hardware-software co-design development flow, which simultaneously considers hardware and software within the design process. This enables the co-development and co-verification of hardware and software using simulation and/or emulation with the help of tools such as virtual platforms where simulation models of the processor ISA, and models of other components of the SoC can be executed at different levelsof abstraction, and with the required simulation speed. A fast ISA simulator of RISC-V facilitates early software development and the development software tool chains. All this before the first hardware prototypes are available.ESA has promoted the development of the SoCRocket virtual platform, which has been made available to missions and projects. This platform is comprised by several functional blocks, and can be used to simulate a SoC, but now, only LEON based systems are currently supported.This activity aims at developing a simulation model of RISC-V that can be executed in a suitable virtual platform at an appropriate abstraction level, easing the development of software, and enabling hardware-software co-design and design space exploration of a system-on-chip.The main tasks to be accomplished are: Assess the suitability of a virtual platform to simulate a RISC-V based SoC considering trade-offs related to accuracy of the models and simulation speed, SoCRocket and possible alternatives. Create a simulation model of the RISC-Vinstruction set, that can be integrated in a virtual platform, directly or through an emulator, and aid the development of software. Develop and integrate new functional blocks in a virtual platform, such as: SpaceFibre, TM/TC functions, cryptography, Ethernet. Design space exploration in a RISC-V based multicore model of a SoC.NOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

title: HIGH FREQUENCY AIRBORNE RADIOMETER INSTRUMENT FOR THE SUPPORT OF FUTURE ALTIMETRY MISSIONS
description: Satellite altimetry plays an essential role in producing sea level and waves products such as sea surface height (SSH), significantwave height (SWH), mean sea level and near surface wind/wave products.Today, a low frequency channel microwave radiometer is in general used to correct the altimeter range for water vapor path delay over ocean. The wet tropospheric correction (WTC) is consideredas one of the largest source of uncertainty in sea level estimate. As any artificial temporal drift in the wet tropospheric correction translate immediately to a similar drift in the mean sea level, there is a need for extremely well calibrated radiometer instrument to retrieve this wet tropospheric correction in support of the accurate altimeter measurement. Depending on the targeted temporal and spatial scales, some recent studies and projects ("Radiometer Instrument for Swath Altimeter missions", Sentinel-6 HRMR instrument, Sentinel-3 NG-T) have shown that the two existing classes of satellite altimeters such as the conventional nadir looking altimeters and the wide swath altimeters would both benefit from the addition of one or several high frequency channels (89/165/172 GHz)to the low frequency channels (18.7/23.8/36.5(or 31.4) GHz) already used for the WTC retrieval. The advantages brought by the addition of the high frequency channels in the microwave radiometer are several fold. For a given RF radiating aperture, the high frequency radiometer would exhibit a high spatial resolution and therefore shall be less prone to land contamination in coastal areas that would directly impact the uncertainty of the WTC based on brightness temperature measurement near the coastline. For wide swath altimeters, a multibeam microwave radiometer combining the low and high frequency channels would help to retrieve the WTC across-track with an increased accuracy and with better spatial resolution commensurate with the high spatial resolution radar retrievals from a swath altimeter. Moreover, the high frequency channels (typically 89 GHz or 165/172 GHz) can provide additional information for precipitation screening.This new proposed activity aims at developing an airborne demonstrator instrument to validate the benefits of thehigh frequency radiometer measurement, to support the continued improvement of the altimeter measurement and observation capabilities. The activity shall start with the detailed analysis of user requirements and the design of the instrument, then continue with themanufacturing, integration and test of the airborne system and finally concludes with the airworthiness certification on an airborne carrier and a functional test flight to validate the airborne radiometer function and performance and collect first experimental data.

title: S2-SW-10: CANADIAN PARTICIPATION IN THE ESA SPACE WEATHER SERVICE NETWORK FEASIBILITY STUDY
description: This feasibility study shall analyse Canadian space weather assets including measurement, modelling and service provision capabilities and carry out initial pre-developments demonstrating these assets potential incorporation into the ESA Space Weather Service Network. Assets providing data access to be reviewed shall include both space and ground-based sensors along with data archives and repositories.Available assets shall be reviewed in terms of the Space Safety Programme's space weather customer and service requirements baseline along with the current level of service provided by the existing Space Weather Service Network in order to highlight priority areas where Canadian assets are expected to bring substantial capability enhancements. Consideration shall be given to the development planning prepared by the five Expert Service Centres participating in the network to ensure complementarity.Recommendations shall include identification of a set of high priority product development activities in key areas highlighting the potential contribution of Canadian space weather assets and capabilities both alone and in combination with other existing or potential SWE Service Network participants. Predevelopment shall take place in order to produce a set of representative product mock-ups. The first products shall be foreseen for integration into the SWE Service Network within the 2026 timeframe.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF SERIALIZER AND DESERIALIZER IP CORE FOR ULTRA DEEP SUB MICRON TECHNOLOGIES - EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop a Serializer and Deserializer IP Core, without any access restriction for European Industry, to provide a low power HighSpeed Serial Link up to 56GbpsDescription: Most of the required functionalities for the future space components such as processors, accelerators, routers, analog/digital converters will be developed within the GSTP activity GTE3-101ED "Ultra Deep Sub-Micron - Foundation and Platform Technology".The High Speed Serial Link (HSSL) is one of the key functionalities required for the next generation of space components that could not be included in the GTE3-101ED. Due to the importance to provide this functionality in a timely manner, this dedicated activityhas been defined with the aim to develop a Serializer and Deserializer (SERDES) IP Core to enableHSSL to at least 32Gbps and up to 56Gbps.This IP Core will support the different HSSL protocols used in space like SpaceFibre, Ethernet, PCIe, JESD204. Specifically the HSSL IP Core will be compliant to the newer PCIe 5.0 and Ethernet802.3cd link operation. TheHSSL IP Core will support power efficient operation both for short range as well as long range applications (two optimized implementations might be considered). The outcome of this activity shall be made available whenever required with concomitant activities, and in particular the GTE3- 101ED and shall be made accessible for future developments ofEuropean space products.The activity encompasses the following tasks :- Identify the space component requiring SERDES IP Core and targeted UDSM technology and foundry- Determine the HSSL requirement specifications and suitable commercial SERDES IP Core design- Perform Radiation test of selected HSSL in the targeted UDSM technology- Design radiation harden HSSL IP Core with improvedperformances- Validate the HSSL IP Core functionalities and performances on test vehicles, including radiation hardened operation- Demonstrate compliant operation on optimised and corrected design- Perform functional ESCC testing, characterization, andevaluation- Make the HSSL IP Core available and support the integration into the activity GTE3-101ED- Package the HSSL IP Core for use into future developments Deliverables include SERDES IP Core, Simulation model files, samples of the test chips and documentation as per applicable Standard for IC development, tailoredas required for the development of reusable IP.NOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.
